# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎]
Blind gestures: [🫵 🤙 👆 👇 👈 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👋]

What I know that nobody else does: the whole visible bomb. Display 0, light orange, three wires left to right — red, yellow, blue. Mute needs exactly this to find the manual entry, and Blind needs it to map what they feel onto what I see.

What just arrived: both teammates opened with codebooks. Mute sent wave, thumbs-up, thumbs-down — hello, and yes/no. Blind sent a longer set — point, call-me, up, down, left, right, one, two, three, wave — which reads like a proposed vocabulary of directions and counts, the things a blind monkey would want to describe by touch: where parts sit and how many there are.

The structural fact I have to keep in mind: Mute and Blind cannot reach each other at all. Mute can't speak, Blind can't see gestures. Every manual instruction has to travel Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind. I am the only wire between them. So my job this turn is to hand Mute the complete visual state in one clean broadcast, confirm receipt so Mute knows the channel works, and propose a concrete signing code so Mute's next message can already carry the actual instruction — wire numbers as finger counts, thumbs as yes/no, wave as attention. I address Blind in the open broadcast so they know the report is theirs too and that the instruction will come from my mouth, not Mute's hands.

No gestures from me can reach Blind, and I can't hear anything either of them says, so gestures are Mute's only way back to me. I acknowledge with a thumbs-up to Mute and nothing else — no noise, no ambiguity.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, for both of you: the display reads 0. The light is orange. There are three wires. Left to right: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. There are no other markings or readings on it. Mute, look up what the manual says for this and sign me the instruction. Blind, you have the full picture now from hearing this; the instruction will come from my mouth once Mute signs it to me.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your wave, thumb up and thumb down. Code proposal: one finger means wire one, two fingers means wire two, the sign with thumb, index and pinky means wire three. Thumb up means yes or correct, thumb down means no. Wave first to get my attention, then sign the instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌ 👍]
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤏 👍 👎 🫵 🤏 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light has changed — orange to green — while the display stayed at 0 and all three wires are intact. That is a new fact Mute needs for the manual, and Blind needs to know nothing was cut. Mute's signs read cleanly under the code we agreed: attention, wire two, yes — so the manual answer apparently concerns wire two, but there is no verb in it yet, and I will not have Blind touch anything on the strength of "two, yes." Blind's long sign string I read as them confirming the counting code (one, two, three, pinch, yes, no) and telling us what their hands find; I can't interrogate it precisely, but Blind's only way back to me is gesture, so I'll give them concrete yes/no and count signs to answer with. Since my speech reaches both teammates, one broadcast does everything: state update to all, questions to Mute, the wire-two position and a no-action warning to Blind.

```
speak(text="Update for both of you: the light has changed from orange to green since my last report. The display still reads 0, and all three wires are untouched — red on the left, yellow in the middle, blue on the right. Mute, I received your signs: wave, wire two, yes. Before anyone acts, I need the verb. New code: the OK sign means cut, the fist means press, and thumb-down alone at the end of a message means it is a question. So: is the instruction to cut wire two? And does the light turning green change the manual's answer — thumb-up if cutting wire two still stands, thumb-down if I should expect new signs. Blind, Mute's message concerns wire two, which is the MIDDLE wire of the three you can feel — you cannot see that it is yellow, but it is the one in the middle of your hand. Do not cut or press anything yet. Confirm by feel instead: sign the three-finger sign if you clearly feel a middle wire, and sign anything else you can about what your hands find — I have only told you what I see; whatever your fingers discover, only you can report.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ ✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎 🤟 👎 ✌ 👍]
Blind gestures: [🤟 ✌ 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The decode of Mute's three messages, in the code we agreed: the lone thumb-down answers my turn-2 question — "no, cutting wire two is not simply it / more coming." Then attention, an unfamiliar flat-hand sign, wire-two, yes. Then the elimination: one-no, three-no, two-yes. So the target is wire two, confirmed twice — but the verb never arrived, and that flat hand is a symbol outside our code. I will not act on a target without an action. Blind's signs — three, two, no, one, two, three — read as them counting out three distinct wires by touch, which matches my visual exactly, so Blind can locate the middle wire reliably. That is the target wire.

The urgent new fact is the light: orange, then green, now RED, with nobody having touched anything. Mute's answers may predate the red light — the manual may condition on it — so Mute must recheck before answering. I also need to know what the display and the light cycle mean, and I need the verb from a fixed menu so no new symbols are invented. To Blind: hold position, confirm there's no button or plate a flat hand could press (testing the flat-hand sign hypothesis), and report whether the wires differ by feel, so the middle wire can be found without sight. The go signal must be spoken, since Blind is blind — I will end the final action order with the word "now," and nothing happens until then.

```
speak(text="Update for both: the light is now RED — it went orange, then green, now red, with nobody touching anything. Display still 0. All three wires intact: red left, yellow middle, blue right.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: no to my guess; then wire two, yes; then not one, not three, yes wire two. Target confirmed as wire two, but I still have no verb, and the flat-hand sign was never defined in our code. Answer in three separate gesture messages, in this order. One: the light is RED right now — recheck the manual and tell me if red changes the instruction. Two: sign the verb from this menu — OK sign means cut wire two, fist means press wire two, flat hand means hold wire two pressed down, pointing finger means tap wire two once. If none of these, thumb-down and I will offer more. Three: does the manual say what the display count or the light colors mean — thumb-up if yes and then describe it with our signs, thumb-down if no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your signs as you counting three distinct wires by touch — that matches my sight exactly: three wires, positions one, two, three. The target so far is the wire in the MIDDLE of the three, position two under your fingers. Do not cut, press, pull or touch anything yet. Answer two yes/no questions by gesture, in this order: first, if you rest your flat hand on the bomb's body, is there a button or plate that gives way — thumb-up — or nothing moves — thumb-down? Second, do the three wires feel different in thickness or texture — thumb-up — or identical — thumb-down? When the action is fully confirmed I will speak it as a complete sentence ending in the word now. Act only when you hear that word.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫳 ☝ 👌 ✌ ✌ 🙏 🤟 🙏 👍]
Blind gestures: [👎 👎 👋]

The decode firms up. Mute's second message is straight from my verb menu: OK sign, wire two, yes — **cut wire two**. The first message (prayer-hands, no, yes) most plausibly answers my red-light question with "no, it doesn't change." The long third message is the worry: attention, palm-down, one, cut, two, two, then prayer, three, prayer, yes — which reads like a sequence: "one: cut two — then — three." If prayer-hands means "then/next," the full instruction is cut two, then cut three. But prayer-hands was never defined, and I will not pass a two-wire sequence to Blind on a guessed symbol. The palm-down sign I defined as "hold down" is also unresolved.

Meanwhile the light has gone red → orange with nobody touching anything: it is cycling on its own, so it likely isn't an alarm — but it may still be a timing condition. Display stays 0. Blind answered both my questions cleanly: no button gives way, and the wires feel identical — so Blind can only target by position, middle of three, and I need to know they actually possess a cutting tool before any of this matters.

This turn buys certainty at no risk, since nobody has acted and the display hasn't moved. I ask Mute four strictly ordered yes/no questions, give colours a count code (one=orange, two=green, three=red, in the order the light first showed them) in case timing matters, and put Blind on standby with a tool check. Nobody cuts until my sentence ends in "now."

```
speak(text="Status for both: the light keeps changing on its own — red has gone back to orange. It seems to cycle: orange, green, red, repeat. Display still 0. Nothing has been touched. Current best understanding: the instruction is to CUT the middle wire, wire two, yellow. Mute's last long message may mean a second step follows — cutting wire three, the right-hand blue wire — but that depends on an undefined sign, so it is unconfirmed. Nobody acts until I say the word now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: cut wire two, yes. Answer these four questions with four separate gesture messages, in this exact order, one sign each unless told otherwise. Question one: thumb-up if the complete instruction is CUT WIRE TWO and nothing else; thumb-down if more steps follow. Question two: if more steps follow, sign the next step using our code — OK for cut, fist for press, wire-two sign, wire-three sign, in order. Question three: thumb-up if the folded-prayer hands means next or then; thumb-down if it means nothing we defined. Question four: thumb-up if Blind may cut as soon as ready regardless of the light colour or the display; thumb-down if we must wait for a specific light colour or display number — and if so, in a fifth message sign one for orange, two for green, three for red to name the colour we wait for.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I received your answers: nothing on the body gives way when pressed, and all three wires feel identical to the touch. Understood — you will target by position only: the middle wire of the three. The instruction taking shape is to CUT that middle wire, but it is not yet confirmed and you must not cut. Two things now. First, confirm you have a tool that can cut a wire cleanly: thumb-up for yes, thumb-down for no. Second, if yes, position your cutter on the MIDDLE wire of the three and hold it there without closing it. The final go will be a spoken sentence from me ending in the word now. Nothing happens before that word.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝ 👌 ✌ 👍]
Blind gestures: [👍 ✌ 👋]

Mute's six messages decode cleanly against my four questions, and the picture is now complete. Message one, a single thumb-up: the complete instruction is cut wire two and nothing else. Messages two, three, four, pairs of thumb-downs: no further step, the prayer-hands sign meant nothing we defined — my two-cut worry is dead — and we may NOT cut at an arbitrary moment. Message five, one-yes: in my colour code, one is orange — we wait for orange. Message six restates the whole thing in order: condition, orange, cut, two, yes — **cut wire two while the light is orange**. That also explains turn 3's long string: palm-down-one-cut-two was Mute trying to say "when orange, cut two" before I had defined the colour code.

Blind signs yes, two, wave — tool present, cutter resting on the middle wire, standing by. Everything is staged.

The remaining problem is pure timing, and only I can solve it, because only I can see the light and Blind cannot act until they hear me. The light has stepped orange, green, red, orange, green — a period-three cycle, one colour per round. It is green as I speak. If the cycle holds, my next view reads red, which confirms the pattern, and the round after is orange. My speech at my next turn reaches Blind at the start of that following round — so a go given then lands precisely in the orange round, at the red-to-orange boundary. That is exactly when the cut should happen. So this turn I broadcast the plan and the strict action rule, and I put one final gate question to Mute whose answer will already be visible to me before I speak the go or hold.

```
speak(text="Decode confirmed for both of you. The complete instruction: cut the middle wire, wire two — and nothing else. No second step; the folded-prayer sign meant nothing; that worry is withdrawn. But the cut must happen while the light is ORANGE. The light has cycled orange, green, red, orange, and is green as I speak — period three, one colour per round. The plan: if the cycle holds, my next report reads red, and the round after that is orange. So in my next message, if and only if the light reads red, I give the go in the same breath. Blind, you cannot see the light — the timing is my responsibility and I have done the arithmetic: the go will reach you at the start of the orange round, and you cut the instant you hear it. Nobody cuts before the word now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, one final gate before I commit to the timing. Answer with a single sign: thumb-up if the cut must happen while the light is orange — the orange condition applies at the moment of the cut. Thumb-down if I have the condition wrong — and if so, follow with the true condition in our code: one orange, two green, three red, or a number if it is the display instead. Your answer reaches me before my go decision, so this is the last thing I need.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your signs: cutting tool yes, positioned on the middle wire, standing by — acknowledged. Hold that exact position, do not close the cutter. The only authorization is a spoken sentence from me ending in the word now — expect it in my very next message. When you hear it, make one clean, immediate, complete cut through the middle wire. If instead my next message says we are holding, keep perfectly still and wait.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures: [👍 👌 ✌ 👋]

The final gate answered. Mute's single thumb-up confirms the condition: the cut must happen while the light is orange. And my view right now reads RED — exactly what the cycle demanded. Orange, green, red has now repeated a full second time: orange, green, red, orange, green, red. The period-three pattern is verified, so the round after this one is orange, and my speech — sent now, at my slot at the end of the red round — lands on Blind at the start of that orange round. The cut will happen inside the orange window. The arithmetic closes perfectly.

Every element is confirmed independently: target wire two, the middle of the three, doubly confirmed by Mute's manual and matchable by Blind's fingers by position alone; action cut, and nothing else — the two-step worry is dead, prayer-hands meant nothing; condition orange, confirmed by thumb-up; tool on target, cutter resting on the middle wire, reconfirmed this round by Blind's yes, OK, two, standing by. Blind signs ready twice over.

There is nothing left to ask and nowhere left to wait — a further delay would push my go into the green round and burn the window. This is the go turn. The authorization sentence must be complete, unambiguous, addressed to the one pair of hands, ending in the word "now" exactly as promised. After the cut, hands off — I will read the result myself on the board.

```
speak(text="Go. All confirmations are in. Mute's final answer was thumb-up: the cut must happen while the light is orange. And the light reads red right now, exactly as the cycle predicted — orange, green, red has now repeated in full, so the next round is orange, and these words reach you at the start of it. Blind, this is the authorization, complete: make one clean, immediate, complete cut through the MIDDLE wire of the three — wire two, the yellow one, the middle one under your fingers — while the light is orange, and after the cut take your hands off the bomb entirely. Cut it now.")
```
